scenes.heading: DAG
scenes.narration: Let's take a deep look at DAG and how it works under the hood in Spark.

scenes.heading: What the DAG represents
items: A Directed Acyclic Graph of RDD/DataFrame dependencies
Built lazily as you chain transformations
Materialized only when an action fires
scenes.narration: The DAG is Spark's internal blueprint of your computation, a directed acyclic graph where each node is a dataset and each edge is a transformation. Because transformations are lazy, Spark simply records dependencies into this graph rather than executing anything. Only when you call an action does Spark hand the completed graph to the scheduler for execution.

scenes.heading: From code to execution
scenes.narration: When an action triggers execution, the DAGScheduler walks the graph backward and cuts it into stages at every shuffle boundary. Narrow dependencies are pipelined together inside a single stage, while wide dependencies force a new stage. Each stage becomes a set of tasks, one per partition, that the TaskScheduler dispatches to executors.

scenes.heading: DAG vs MapReduce

left.title: Spark DAG
points: Multi-stage plan optimized as a whole

scenes.narration: Unlike MapReduce, which forces every job into a rigid map-then-reduce shape and spills to disk between steps, the DAG lets Spark reason about the entire pipeline at once. That whole-plan view is what enables pipelining of narrow operations and keeping intermediate results in memory. The result is far fewer disk round-trips and dramatically faster iterative workloads.

scenes.code:
df = spark.read.parquet("/data/sales")
filtered = df.filter(df.region == "EMEA")
agg = filtered.groupBy("product").sum("amount")
agg.explain(True)  # inspect the plan
agg.write.parquet("/out/emea")  # action triggers DAG
scenes.heading: Inspecting the DAG
scenes.narration: Here the read, filter, and groupBy calls only build up the DAG; nothing runs yet. The filter is a narrow transformation, while groupBy introduces a shuffle and therefore a stage boundary. Calling explain lets you see the logical and physical plans Spark derived from the graph. The write action is what finally submits the DAG to the scheduler and executes it.

scenes.text: The DAG is the source of truth for stages, tasks, and optimization.
scenes.narration: Whenever you debug performance, start by reading the DAG and its stage boundaries in the Spark UI. Every shuffle you see there is a chance to reduce data movement.
